abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

achaia.title: Achaia
achaia.note: The Roman province covering southern Greece, with Corinth in it, where Paul spent a long stretch and wrote back afterwards.

agabus.title: Agabus
agabus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
agabus.note: A prophet at Antioch who said a severe famine was coming. It came in the reign of Claudius, and the church sent relief to the believers in Judea.

alexander-2.title: Alexander
alexander-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
alexander-2.note: A man from the New Testament, and Acts is the only book that names him.

amphipolis.title: Amphipolis
amphipolis.note: Paul and Silas passed through on the road from Philippi to Thessalonica. It was a major Macedonian city on the Strymon River and a Roman administrative centre on the Via Egnatia, and its Greek and Roman remains, a lion monument among them, have been excavated.

antioch.title: Antioch
antioch.note: Antioch on the Orontes, in Syria, the third largest city of the Roman Empire. Believers were first called Christians there, and its church sent Paul out on his journeys. It survives as the Turkish city of Antakya.

antioch-2.title: Antioch
antioch-2.note: The other Antioch, in Pisidia. Paul preached there with some success until local Jewish leaders drove him out, and later he came back to strengthen the church.

apollonia.title: Apollonia
apollonia.note: A stop on the Via Egnatia between Amphipolis and Thessalonica, passed through by Paul and Silas on the way from Philippi.

apollos.title: Apollos
apollos.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
apollos.note: An eloquent Jewish preacher from Alexandria who knew the Scriptures and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only John's baptism. Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and explained the way of God more fully. In Corinth he did so well that a faction started claiming him over Paul.

aquila.title: Aquila
aquila.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
aquila.note: A Jewish tentmaker from Pontus. He and his wife Priscilla had been expelled from Rome with other Jews, met Paul in Corinth, and worked beside him. Churches met in their home in more than one city.

areopagite.title: Areopagite
areopagite.note: Dionysius was one, a member of the old council of Athens that met on the rock of the Areopagus. He was among the few Athenians who believed after Paul spoke there.

areopagus.title: Areopagus
areopagus.note: Mars' Hill. It was a rocky outcrop below the Acropolis in Athens and also the council of leading magistrates that met on it. Paul was brought before them to explain what he taught about Jesus and the resurrection, and gave his speech about the unknown god.

aristarchus.title: Aristarchus
aristarchus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
aristarchus.note: A Macedonian who travelled with Paul. He was dragged into the riot at Ephesus, sailed with Paul to Rome, and was imprisoned with him there.

asia.title: Asia
asia.note: Not the continent. The Roman province of Asia, in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus among its churches, and the region the seven churches of Revelation belonged to.

assos.title: Assos
assos.note: Paul walked to Assos while his companions sailed round, and he met them there on the way to Jerusalem. It was an Aegean port in Mysia, facing Lesbos. The ruins, a Doric temple of Athena among them, still stand above the Turkish village of Behramkale.

athenian.title: Athenian
athenian.note: Luke notes that Athenians loved anything new, just before Paul's speech to the philosophers on the Areopagus, where he used their own poets and altars to speak of the God they worshipped without knowing.

athens.title: Athens
athens.note: The intellectual capital of the Greek world. Paul's sermon on the Areopagus there, quoting Greek poets and arguing with Greek philosophy while preaching the resurrection, is one of the most carefully fitted speeches in Acts.

attalia.title: Attalia
attalia.note: Paul and Barnabas sailed home to Antioch from this port in Pamphylia at the end of their first journey. Attalus II Philadelphus of Pergamon founded it and named it for himself. It is Antalya now, and parts of the old harbour and wall are still standing.

barjesus.title: Barjesus
barjesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
barjesus.note: A Jewish false prophet and magician who had attached himself to Sergius Paulus, the Roman proconsul of Cyprus. He also went by Elymas. He tried to turn the proconsul away from the faith and was struck blind for it.

barnabas.title: Barnabas
barnabas.about: Levite living at the time of the New Testament
barnabas.note: Joseph was his given name. He was a Levite from Cyprus. The apostles called him Barnabas, son of encouragement, after he sold a field and gave the money to the Jerusalem church.

barsabas-2.title: Barsabas
barsabas-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
barsabas-2.note: A surname, son of Sabas. This is Judas Barsabas, sent with Silas to carry the council's letter to Antioch.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

berea.title: Berea
berea.note: It was in Macedonia, and Paul and Silas went there after a mob drove them out of Thessalonica. Luke commends the Bereans for checking the Scriptures every day against what Paul taught.

bithynia.title: Bithynia
bithynia.note: A Roman province on the south shore of the Black Sea. Paul tried to go there and the Spirit stopped him. By the time Peter wrote his first letter there were Christians there anyway.

blastus.title: Blastus
blastus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
blastus.note: Herod Agrippa I's chamberlain. The people of Tyre and Sidon won him over and got him to help patch things up with the angry king.

caesar-2.title: Caesar
caesar-2.about: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
caesar-2.note: In Acts the title stands for the emperor of the day, the authority whose court the appeal in Acts 25 went to.

caesarea.title: Caesarea
caesarea.note: Herod the Great built it as a Roman port on the Mediterranean coast, and it served as the administrative capital of Roman Judea. Cornelius the centurion lived there. Paul spent two years there in prison.

cencrea.title: Cencrea
cencrea.note: Corinth's eastern harbour on the Saronic Gulf, about seven miles from the city. Paul cut his hair there for a vow before he sailed, and the town had a church of its own.

chanaan.title: Chanaan
chanaan.note: The King James spelling of Canaan in Acts, where Stephen's speech looks back on the land promised to Abraham's descendants.

chios.title: Chios
chios.note: A big Aegean island off Asia Minor, still called Chios, that Paul's ship sailed past on the way home from the third missionary journey.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

christian.title: Christian
christian.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christian.note: Outsiders at Antioch coined the word, possibly as mockery, for people who followed Christ. The believers called each other brethren, disciples and saints. It turns up only three times in the New Testament, the last in 1 Peter 4:16, which tells them not to be ashamed of suffering under that name.

cilicia.title: Cilicia
cilicia.note: Paul was born in Tarsus, Cilicia's chief city, on the southeastern coast of Asia Minor. Cilician Jews had their own synagogue in Jerusalem and argued with Stephen there. The province was known for the goat's hair cloth used in tentmaking, which was Paul's trade.

cis.title: Cis
cis.about: Saul's father living at the time of United Monarchy
cis.note: Kish, Saul's father, in the Greek form Paul uses once in his sermon at Pisidian Antioch.

claudius.title: Claudius
claudius.about: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
claudius.note: The emperor who threw the Jews out of Rome, which is how Priscilla and Aquila came to Corinth and met Paul. A famine in his reign moved the church at Antioch to send help to the believers in Judea.

corinth.title: Corinth
corinth.note: Paul stayed eighteen months in this rich trading city on the isthmus, and the church he planted got two of his longest letters. He stood before the proconsul Gallio there, whose dated term helps fix Paul's timeline. An inscription found at Corinth names an Erastus who paid for a pavement, likely the city treasurer of Romans 16:23.

corinthian.title: Corinthian
corinthian.note: Anyone from Corinth. Crispus, the synagogue ruler who believed with his household, is one Acts names, and Paul speaks straight to them as Corinthians in his second letter.

crispus.title: Crispus
crispus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
crispus.note: He ran the synagogue at Corinth, believed under Paul's preaching, and was one of the few Corinthians Paul baptised himself.

cyprus.title: Cyprus
cyprus.note: The island Barnabas came from, where the first missionary journey started and the proconsul Sergius Paulus became an early convert.

damaris.title: Damaris
damaris.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
damaris.note: An Athenian woman who believed after Paul spoke at the Areopagus, one of the very few converts from that speech named at all. Dionysius the Areopagite is named in the same verse, and nothing ties the two together beyond that.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

demetrius.title: Demetrius
demetrius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
demetrius.note: A silversmith in Ephesus who made shrines of Artemis. He saw Paul's preaching killing his trade and started a riot, and the crowd chanted for two hours before the city officials calmed it.

derbe.title: Derbe
derbe.note: Paul and Barnabas fled here from Lystra after Paul was stoned, and Paul came back later. It was a small town in the Lycaonian highlands near modern Karaman, and the hometown of Gaius. An inscription found in 1956 at Kerti Höyük fixed the site.

diana.title: Diana
diana.about: A female deity in the New Testament
diana.note: The Latin name for Artemis, goddess of Ephesus. When silversmiths feared Paul was ruining the shrine trade, the city chanted for two hours that great is Artemis of the Ephesians.

dionysius.title: Dionysius
dionysius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
dionysius.note: A member of the Areopagus, the council of Athens, who believed after hearing Paul speak there.

easter.title: Easter
easter.note: The King James has Easter once, at Acts 12:4, and the Greek word underneath it is pascha, Passover. Every later translation says so.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

elymas.title: Elymas
elymas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
elymas.note: Bar-Jesus, a Jewish false prophet on Cyprus, also called Elymas, which means sorcerer. He tried to turn the proconsul Sergius Paulus away from the faith. Paul struck him blind for a time, and the proconsul believed.

ephesus.title: Ephesus
ephesus.note: The chief city of Roman Asia, with the temple of Artemis and a theatre for some twenty five thousand. Paul stayed about three years and the silversmiths rioted over lost trade. Later it was one of the seven churches of Revelation, and tradition says John died and was buried there.

epicurean.title: Epicurean
epicurean.about: Philosophical group in the New Testament
epicurean.note: Followers of Epicurus, who taught that the best thing in life is pleasure, meaning freedom from pain and worry, and that the gods, if there are any, leave people alone. Some of them argued with Paul in Athens, along with Stoics.

erastus.title: Erastus
erastus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
erastus.note: Paul's companion, and in Romans the city treasurer of Corinth. An inscription found at Corinth names an Erastus who paid for a pavement in return for an aedileship.

eutychus.title: Eutychus
eutychus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
eutychus.note: Asleep in a third-storey window at Troas while Paul preached late, he fell to the ground and was taken up for dead. Paul went down, held him and said he was alive, and they went back up and ate and talked until daybreak.

gaius-3.title: Gaius
gaius-3.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
gaius-3.note: Acts names him once, and he is a man from the New Testament.

gaius-4.title: Gaius
gaius-4.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
gaius-4.note: One of 4 men called Gaius. This one is a man from the New Testament, named once in Acts.

galilee.title: Galilee
galilee.note: Jesus grew up here and did most of his public work around the Sea of Galilee. Judeans thought the north provincial and mixed, which is the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come out of Nazareth.

gallio.title: Gallio
gallio.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
gallio.note: The proconsul of Achaia threw out the case the Jews of Corinth brought against Paul, calling it an internal religious quarrel and no business of his court. An inscription from Delphi naming Gallio dates the scene closely enough to anchor the chronology of Paul's whole ministry.

gentile.title: Gentile
gentile.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
gentile.note: Anyone who is not Jewish. The Greek word behind it means nation or people, and Paul's gospel turns on Gentiles being grafted into God's covenant people without first becoming Jews, the position defended at the Jerusalem council in Acts 15.

grecian.title: Grecian
grecian.note: Greek-speaking Jews, as against Hebrew-speaking ones. They complained that their widows were losing out in the daily food, and that is how Stephen and six others came to be appointed.

greece.title: Greece
greece.note: Paul spent three months here near the end of his third journey. The Old Testament calls the region and its people Javan. Athens, Corinth and Philippi were Greek cities where Paul planted churches.

greek-2.title: Greek
greek-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
greek-2.note: Used of a woman. Mark calls the Syrophoenician mother who begged Jesus to heal her daughter a Greek, meaning a Gentile, not Greek by birth. The honourable Greek women at Berea who believed Paul get the same word.

hermes.title: Hermes
hermes.about: A male deity in the New Testament
hermes.note: In Acts 14:12 a crowd decides Paul must be Hermes, the messenger of the Greek gods, because he was the one doing the talking. The Roman Christian of the same name in Romans 16:14 is someone else.

herod.title: Herod
herod.about: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
herod.note: Herod Antipas, the son of Herod the Great. He ruled Galilee through Jesus's ministry and beheaded John the Baptist for condemning his marriage, and Luke has him mock Jesus before the crucifixion.

herod-3.title: Herod
herod-3.about: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
herod-3.note: Herod Agrippa the First, the grandson. He executed the apostle James and put Peter in prison.

iconium.title: Iconium
iconium.note: Modern Konya, in central Asia Minor. Paul and Barnabas came here after being thrown out of Antioch in Pisidia, and a crowd of Jews and Gentiles turned on them, so they fled to Lystra and Derbe. Paul came back later to strengthen the church.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

israelite.title: Israelite
israelite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israelite.note: One of the people descended from Jacob, who was renamed Israel. Paul calls himself an Israelite in Romans 11 when he argues God has not dropped his people.

italy.title: Italy
italy.note: Aquila and Priscilla had just come from Italy when Paul met them, after Claudius threw the Jews out of Rome. Paul later went there as a prisoner, by way of a shipwreck. Hebrews ends with greetings from "those from Italy".

james.title: James
james.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
james.note: Zebedee's son and John's older brother. He was one of the three closest to Jesus, and the first of the twelve to be killed, by Herod Agrippa the First.

james-2.title: James
james-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
james-2.note: The brother of Jesus. He did not believe during the ministry, then led the Jerusalem church after the resurrection, and the letter of James is traditionally his.

jason.title: Jason
jason.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jason.note: Paul and Silas stayed with him in Thessalonica. When a mob came for Paul and could not find him, they dragged Jason before the city officials instead, charging him with harbouring men who defied Caesar's decrees, and he had to post bond to go free.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

john-2.title: John
john-2.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
john-2.note: Zebedee's son and James's younger brother, a fisherman, and with Peter and James one of the three who saw what the rest did not, the transfiguration and Gethsemane among it. From the cross Jesus gave him his mother Mary to look after. Tradition makes him the disciple Jesus loved and credits him with the fourth Gospel, three letters, and Revelation, written in exile on Patmos.

john.title: John
john.about: Prophet living at the time of the New Testament
john.note: The prophet who comes out of the wilderness in Matthew 3, preaching repentance and baptising. Jesus came to him to be baptised. Later, from prison, he sent his own disciples to ask whether Jesus was the one.

joppa.title: Joppa
joppa.note: Judea's main seaport, a point of land on the Mediterranean. Jonah sailed from there running from Nineveh, and cedar for Solomon's and Zerubbabel's temples came ashore there. In Acts, Peter raised Tabitha at Joppa and, staying with Simon the tanner, had the vision that opened the gospel to Gentiles.

judaea.title: Judaea
judaea.note: The Roman name for the southern part of the land around Jerusalem, roughly old Judah. Client kings of Herod's family ruled it, then Roman procurators like Pontius Pilate. John the Baptist preached in its wilderness and the Passion happened there. After the revolt of AD 66 to 70 Rome struck coins reading "Judaea Capta."

jupiter.title: Jupiter
jupiter.about: A male deity in the New Testament
jupiter.note: At Lystra, after Paul healed a man lame from birth, the crowd decided Barnabas was Jupiter and Paul was Mercury. The priest of Jupiter brought oxen to sacrifice to them, and the two tore their clothes to stop it. Jupiter was the Greeks' Zeus, the chief god.

justus.title: Justus
justus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
justus.note: A second name several early Christians carried. One was a man in Corinth whose house stood next door to the synagogue, and Paul used it as a meeting place.

lucius.title: Lucius
lucius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
lucius.note: One of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch, from Cyrene, there when the Holy Spirit set Barnabas and Saul apart. Paul sends greetings from a Lucius he calls his kinsman in Romans 16:21, and whether that is the same man is uncertain.

lycaonia.title: Lycaonia
lycaonia.note: Inland Asia Minor, between Cappadocia and Galatia, with Iconium, Lystra and Derbe in it. Paul and Barnabas preached through it on the first journey. The crowd at Lystra shouted in "the speech of Lycaonia" when they took the two for Hermes and Zeus, and an inscription found near Lystra shows those two gods really were worshipped together there.

lydia.title: Lydia
lydia.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
lydia.note: She sold purple cloth, came from Thyatira, and lived in Philippi when Paul arrived. She already worshipped God, and after hearing Paul by the river she and her household were baptised, apparently the first converts in Europe. Then she put Paul and his companions up in her house.

lystra.title: Lystra
lystra.note: A Roman colony in the wild hills of Lycaonia, and Timothy's hometown. Paul healed a man lame from birth there and the crowd tried to sacrifice to him and Barnabas as Hermes and Zeus. Then Paul's opponents turned the same crowd, and they stoned him and left him for dead.

macedonia.title: Macedonia
macedonia.note: The Roman province over northern Greece. Paul crossed into it after a vision of a man pleading, "Come over into Macedonia and help us," and went on through Philippi, Thessalonica and Berea, where Christian mission in Europe is usually said to begin. He came back at least twice and praised its churches for giving out of their poverty.

manaen.title: Manaen
manaen.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
manaen.note: A prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch, with Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene and Saul. That group laid hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them out. Luke adds that Manaen grew up alongside Herod Antipas, the man who had John the Baptist killed.

marcus.title: Marcus
marcus.about: Levite living at the time of the New Testament
marcus.note: John Mark. He set out with Paul and Barnabas and left partway through the first journey, and that later split the two men in a sharp quarrel. Peter calls him his son, and early church tradition says he wrote the Gospel of Mark from Peter's preaching.

mary-4.title: Mary
mary-4.about: Barnabus' relative living at the time of the New Testament
mary-4.note: A man from the New Testament, and Acts is the only book that names him.

miletus.title: Miletus
miletus.note: About thirty-five miles south of Ephesus, a port in Ionia. Paul, hurrying to be in Jerusalem for Pentecost, called the elders of Ephesus down to Miletus and gave them his farewell, warning of false teachers to come. He later left Trophimus there sick. Silt from the Meander River has since pushed the coast away, and the old theatre now stands miles inland.

mitylene.title: Mitylene
mitylene.note: Paul's ship put in for a night at Mitylene, the chief city of Lesbos, as he hurried to reach Jerusalem before Pentecost. The classical world knew it as the home of the poets Sappho and Alcaeus.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

mysia.title: Mysia
mysia.note: The northwest corner of the province of Asia. The Spirit kept Paul's party from turning aside, so they passed through Mysia without preaching and came down to Troas, where Paul saw the man from Macedonia in a vision.

neapolis.title: Neapolis
neapolis.note: "New city," the port for Philippi on the coast of Macedonia. Paul, Silas, Timothy and Luke landed there from Troas, their first step in Europe, and walked the Via Egnatia about ten miles inland to Philippi. The town is Kavala in Greece today.

niger.title: Niger
niger.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
niger.note: Simeon's Latin surname, meaning "black." He was one of the prophets and teachers at Antioch who sent Paul and Barnabas off on their first missionary journey.

pamphylia.title: Pamphylia
pamphylia.note: Jews from Pamphylia were in Jerusalem at Pentecost. The province lay on the south coast of Asia Minor between Lycia and Cilicia. Paul and Barnabas came ashore at its capital, Perga.

paphos.title: Paphos
paphos.note: The Roman capital of Cyprus, where the governor lived. On their first journey Paul and Barnabas came here and faced down the sorcerer Elymas in front of the proconsul Sergius Paulus.

paul.title: Paul
paul.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
paul.note: Born Saul, a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin and a Roman citizen from Tarsus. He trained as a Pharisee under Gamaliel and hunted the early church. Then the risen Christ met him in a blinding vision.

pentecost.title: Pentecost
pentecost.note: The harvest festival fifty days after Passover. It is the day the Spirit came down on the disciples in Jerusalem. Peter preached, and that is where the church starts.

perga.title: Perga
perga.note: Capital of Pamphylia, on the Cestrus River a few miles in from the sea. Paul and Barnabas landed here on their first journey. It was at Perga that John Mark turned back and went home.

peter.title: Peter
peter.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
peter.note: A Galilean fisherman named Simon. Jesus renamed him Cephas, or Peter, which means rock. He became the most prominent of the twelve and the first to confess Jesus as the Messiah.

pharisee.title: Pharisee
pharisee.about: Religious group in the New Testament
pharisee.note: A Jewish movement devoted to strict keeping of the law, the written text and a large body of oral tradition around it. They carried real weight in the religious life of the people. They argue with Jesus again and again.

phenice.title: Phenice
phenice.note: The King James spelling of Phoenicia, the narrow coast north of Israel where Tyre and Sidon traded. Believers scattered after Stephen's death took the gospel there.

philippi.title: Philippi
philippi.note: Paul came here after a vision of a man of Macedonia asking for help. Philippi was a Roman colony, founded by Philip II and later settled with veteran soldiers under Augustus, and it carried itself like a small Rome.

phrygia.title: Phrygia
phrygia.note: A big inland region of Asia Minor, with Colossae, Hierapolis, Laodicea and Iconium among its cities. Jews from Phrygia heard the apostles at Pentecost. Paul went through the region more than once.

pilate.title: Pilate
pilate.about: Ruler living at the time of the New Testament
pilate.note: Pontius Pilate, Roman governor of Judea. He said three times that he found no guilt in Jesus, and then gave the crowd and the religious leaders what they wanted and had him crucified.

pisidia.title: Pisidia
pisidia.note: Rough country north of Pamphylia, with the Taurus mountains running through it. Paul and Barnabas crossed it on their first journey and preached at Antioch of Pisidia going out and coming back.

priscilla.title: Priscilla
priscilla.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
priscilla.note: Usually named with her husband Aquila. They were tentmakers and church leaders who worked alongside Paul in several cities and hosted a church in their home. Together they took the eloquent Apollos aside and explained the way of God to him more accurately.

rhoda.title: Rhoda
rhoda.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
rhoda.note: A servant girl in the house of Mary, mother of John Mark, where the believers were praying for Peter. When Peter turned up at the gate after the angel freed him, she was so glad she forgot to open it.

rome.title: Rome
rome.note: Capital of the empire that ruled Judea through the whole New Testament period. Paul wrote to the church there, and Acts ends with him in the city as a prisoner, his case appealed to Caesar.

salamis.title: Salamis
salamis.note: The first stop Paul and Barnabas made on their first journey. It was a big port on the east coast of Cyprus, and they preached in its synagogues.

samaria.title: Samaria
samaria.note: Omri bought a hill from a man called Shemer and built a capital on it. Samaria took over from Tirzah as the seat of the northern kingdom. Ahab and the kings after him ruled from there.

samos.title: Samos
samos.note: Paul's ship passed the island on the run from Assos to Miletus. Samos sits in the Aegean off Asia Minor, and in the ancient world it was known for its temple to Hera.

samothracia.title: Samothracia
samothracia.note: A high, mountainous island in the northern Aegean, off Thrace, that sailors steered by. Paul's ship anchored there for a night on the way to Europe.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

saul-2.title: Saul
saul-2.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
saul-2.note: Paul's name before the road to Damascus. Acts keeps calling him Saul for some time after he turned, and the rest of his story is under Paul.

saul.title: Saul
saul.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
saul.note: Israel's first king, found while he was out looking for his father's lost donkeys and anointed by Samuel in private before the tribes confirmed him.

sceva.title: Sceva
sceva.about: Priest living at the time of the New Testament
sceva.note: Acts calls him a chief priest. No high priest of that name appears in the records, so it probably means he stood high among the Jews of Ephesus.

secundus.title: Secundus
secundus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
secundus.note: He came from Thessalonica and travelled with Paul through Macedonia near the end of the third missionary journey, and Acts 20:4 is the only place he is named.

seleucia.title: Seleucia
seleucia.note: The port of Antioch, near the mouth of the Orontes River, where Paul and Barnabas set sail at the start of their first missionary journey.

sergius.title: Sergius
sergius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
sergius.note: Sergius Paulus was the Roman proconsul of Cyprus. He sent for Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God, and he believed after he watched Paul strike the sorcerer Elymas blind. An inscription found on Cyprus names him.

silas.title: Silas
silas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
silas.note: A leader in the Jerusalem church who went with Paul on his second missionary journey, after Paul and Barnabas split up. He is probably the Silvanus of Paul's letters.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

simeon-3.title: Simeon
simeon-3.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
simeon-3.note: A man from the New Testament, and Acts is the only book that names him.

simon.title: Simon
simon.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
simon.note: Simon Peter, called from his fishing in Matthew 4:18 and named first among the twelve apostles. In Matthew 16:16 he is the one who answers the question.

sopater.title: Sopater
sopater.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
sopater.note: A Christian from Berea, son of Pyrrhus, who travelled with Paul through Macedonia carrying the collection for the Jerusalem church.

sosthenes.title: Sosthenes
sosthenes.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
sosthenes.note: The ruler of the synagogue in Corinth, seized and beaten in front of the judgment seat after Gallio threw out the case against Paul.

stephen.title: Stephen
stephen.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
stephen.note: He was picked as one of seven to oversee the food for the Greek-speaking widows in the Jerusalem church. He soon became known for miracles and bold debate instead.

stoick.title: Stoick
stoick.about: Philosophical group in the New Testament
stoick.note: Not a person. The Stoics followed the Greek school Zeno of Citium founded, which taught self-control and calm acceptance of fate, and some of them argued with Paul in Athens (Acts 17:18).

syria.title: Syria
syria.note: The region northeast of Israel, called Aram in the Old Testament. In the New Testament Antioch was its chief city and the base Paul's journeys started from, and Luke dates Jesus's birth by a census under Quirinius.

tarsus.title: Tarsus
tarsus.note: Paul was born here, in the capital of Cilicia on the Cydnus River, about twelve miles from the sea, and he called it no mean city. It had schools of philosophy and rhetoric that rivalled Athens and Alexandria.

thessalonian.title: Thessalonian
thessalonian.note: Someone from Thessalonica, the port in Roman Macedonia where Paul planted a church and then had to leave in a hurry. His two letters to them are among the earliest writing in the New Testament.

thessalonica.title: Thessalonica
thessalonica.note: The capital of Macedonia, a busy port on the Via Egnatia. Paul preached in the synagogue there for a few weeks before opposition drove him on to Berea. Luke calls the city officials politarchs, an unusual title.

thyatira.title: Thyatira
thyatira.note: A trading city in the Roman province of Asia, known for its guilds, especially the dyers. Lydia, the seller of purple cloth Paul met at Philippi, came from there, and Revelation sends one of its seven letters to the church there.

timotheus.title: Timotheus
timotheus.note: Timothy, from Lystra, with a Jewish mother and a Greek father. Paul took him along on his travels and trusted him with hard errands to churches in trouble, and two of Paul's letters are addressed to him.

troas.title: Troas
troas.note: It was a port on the northwest coast of Asia Minor near old Troy. Paul had his vision of the Macedonian man there, come over and help us, and on a later visit he raised Eutychus from the dead during a sermon that went all night.

trophimus.title: Trophimus
trophimus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
trophimus.note: A Gentile from Ephesus who traveled with Paul. People in Jerusalem thought Paul had taken him into the temple, and that started the riot that ended with Paul under arrest.

tychicus.title: Tychicus
tychicus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
tychicus.note: He carried Paul's letters, Ephesians and Colossians among them, and told the churches in person how Paul was doing.

tyrannus.title: Tyrannus
tyrannus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
tyrannus.note: After the synagogue in Ephesus put Paul out, he taught every day for two years in the lecture hall of Tyrannus. Whether Tyrannus was a Jewish teacher or a Greek who rented out the room is not said.
